title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: What the Market Is Pricing In

epigraph.quote: A great company is not automatically a great stock at any price; the entry multiple decides how much of tomorrow's science you get paid for today.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Desk

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 session close of $1,347.11 (and $1,374.45 in the November 23 live snapshot), Eli Lilly commands an equity market capitalization of $1.29 trillion and an enterprise value of $1.33 trillion [35][36]. That valuation prices Lilly at 44.95x trailing P/E, 27.00x forward P/E, 28.65x EV/EBITDA, 15.40x EV/Sales, and 65.47x Price-to-Free-Cash-Flow [35][36]. Put differently, buyers at $1,347.11 accept a trailing free cash flow yield of just 1.53% while the 10-year U.S. Treasury yields 5.04%—a negative 351-basis-point cash-yield spread.

Why does the market pay 65.5x free cash flow for a pharmaceutical manufacturer? Investors are capitalizing three assumptions at once [4][33]. First, they assume tirzepatide (Mounjaro and Zepbound, now 65.9% of Q3 2026 revenue) sustains +30% volume compounding without triggering a price war [34]. Second, they assume oral Foundayo and triple-agonist retatrutide extend the obesity monopoly past 2035 [7][9]. Third, they treat the $8.44 billion in 9M 2026 manufacturing CapEx and $18.24 billion in 9M 2026 BD/M&A outlays as temporary growth investments rather than recurring maintenance and pipeline-replacement costs [33].

web_blocks.takeaway: Reverse DCF shows $1,347.11 already prices 18.5% five-year revenue compounding and 32% steady-state FCF margins, leaving only +7.6% upside to a realistic $1,450.00 base fair value.

web_blocks.the_number: $1,450.00 per share 12-month Base Fair Value (implied equity value ~$1,365B, or 48.0x normalized FY2027E FCF of ~$28.4B / 26.0x FY2027E EPS of ~$55.80).
web_blocks.how_calculated: We project FY2026E revenue of $89.5B and FY2027E revenue of $109.2B (+22.0% YoY, reflecting +34% volume growth offset by -12% realized net price erosion). Applying a 26.0% normalized FCF margin (ex-lumpy upfront M&A) yields $28.4B in FY2027E FCF. Valuing that cash stream at 48.0x FCF (a compression from 65.5x as IRA 2028 approaches) produces $1,363B in equity value, or $1,448–$1,450 across 941.2M diluted shares.
web_blocks.the_inputs: FY2026E revenue $89.5B; FY2027E revenue $109.2B; consolidated realized price erosion -12% YoY; normalized FCF margin 26.0% (accounting for ongoing $10B+/yr CapEx and Chugai royalties); gross debt $49.50B; diluted shares 941.2M; US10Y 5.04%.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear Case $1,050.00 (-22.1%, modeling -20% GLP-1 price erosion trimming FY27E revenue to ~$102.0B and recurring $7.50B/yr Acquired IPR&D compressing economic FCF toward ~$19.0B–$25.0B at 40x–45x); Base Case $1,450.00 (48.0x normalized FY27E FCF of $28.4B); Bull Case $1,720.00 (55x $29.4B FCF if retatrutide Phase 3 data expands TAM without rebate drag).
web_blocks.if_off: If consolidated net pricing stabilizes above -5% YoY and oral Foundayo captures >$5B in 2027 sales without cannibalizing Zepbound margins, fair value shifts toward $1,650–$1,720. Conversely, if 9M 2026's $18.24B M&A pace and $7.50B/yr Acquired IPR&D become permanent pipeline maintenance alongside -20% price erosion, fair value drops to $1,050 (or ~$910/sh at 45x $19.03B economic FCF).

web_blocks.caption: Eli Lilly (LLY) vs. Large-Cap Biopharma Peers: Same-Session Valuation, Profitability & Stage 2 Matrix
web_blocks.takeaway: LLY commands 45.2x TTM P/E and 32.1x P/B—a massive premium over VRTX (34.3x P/E) and REGN—forcing investors to pay peak multiples for growth that is already decelerating on price.

web_blocks.html: Comparing Lilly against large-cap biopharma peers makes the valuation asymmetry clear [35][36]. Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) trades at 34.27x TTM P/E (26.69x forward P/E) and 42.17x P/FCF (though VRTX is Stage 3 / REJECTED in our 2026-11-20 batch), while Regeneron (REGN) trades near 20.7x P/E [35]. Both peers carry far lower single-molecule price-erosion risk and require zero $50B debt-funded CapEx blitzes to defend their franchises.

The market is also underpricing three balance-sheet and regulatory drags exposed in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q [33]. First, gross debt climbed to $49,503 million following May 2026's $8.94 billion net bond issuance [31][33]. Second, accrued sales rebates and discounts surged +39% year-to-date to $24,170 million, underscoring intensifying PBM and payer rebate pressure [33]. Third, HHS selected both Trulicity and Verzenio (15.4% of FY2025 revenue) in January 2026 for IRA Medicare price-setting effective 2028, creating a visible multi-billion-dollar revenue cliff inside our five-year DCF window [33].

book_paragraphs: When a stock crosses a trillion dollars in market value, arithmetic turns ruthless. At the November 20, 2026 closing price of $1,347.11, Eli Lilly is worth $1.29 trillion in equity and $1.33 trillion in enterprise value. That price tag equates to 45 times trailing earnings, 27 times forward earnings, 28.7 times EBITDA, and 65.5 times trailing free cash flow.

To understand what 65.5 times free cash flow actually means, flip the fraction upside down. You are receiving a 1.53 percent trailing free cash flow yield on a stock whose benchmark risk-free alternative—the 10-year U.S. Treasury—currently pays 5.04 percent. That negative 351-basis-point yield spread demands near-flawless execution for half a decade just to earn back the opportunity cost of waiting.

Our reverse discounted cash flow model reveals exactly what buyers at $1,347.11 must believe. They have to underwrite roughly 18.5 percent annual revenue compounding through 2031, taking Lilly from $65 billion in 2025 to more than $200 billion in annual sales. At the same time, they must assume normalized free cash flow margins expand above 32 percent, even while the company pours $8.4 billion into nine-month CapEx and another $18.24 billion into nine-month business development and IPR&D acquisitions.

When we re-underwrite those assumptions using Q3 2026 filing data, the math tightens noticeably. Consolidated realized net prices dropped 15 percent year-over-year in the third quarter, led by a 29 percent price drop outside the United States after Mounjaro entered China's national reimbursement list. Meanwhile, tirzepatide has climbed to 65.9 percent of total revenue, and Washington selected both Trulicity and Verzenio—15.4 percent of 2025 sales—for 2028 Medicare price-setting under the Inflation Reduction Act.

If we model realistic 2027 revenue of $109.2 billion, a 26 percent normalized free cash flow margin ($28.4 billion), and a 48x exit multiple as 2028 IRA headwinds come into view, we arrive at a 12-month Base Fair Value of $1,450.00 per share. From $1,347.11, that represents just 7.6 percent upside against a technical invalidation stop of $1,172.53 (-13.0 percent)—a sub-1:1 reward-to-risk ratio.

book_subsections.title: Why Peer Multiples and Balance-Sheet Friction Matter
paragraphs: Against Vertex Pharmaceuticals at 34.3 times trailing earnings and Regeneron near 21 times, Eli Lilly's 45.2x trailing multiple leaves zero room for margin slippage. Vertex generates high-margin cystic fibrosis cash flows without carrying $49.5 billion of gross debt or $24.17 billion in accrued rebate liabilities.

Even if Lilly's oral GLP-1 Foundayo scales rapidly in 2027, Chugai Pharmaceutical collects a mid-single-digit to low-teens tiered royalty directly inside Cost of Sales. Add $7.54 billion in nine-month nondeductible IPR&D that pushed Lilly's Q3 effective tax rate to 23.3 percent, and the gap between headline non-GAAP excitement and owner-level free cash flow widens.

Look closely at the capital cost behind Lilly's growth. Nine-month business development and M&A outlays reached $18.24 billion alongside $8.44 billion in manufacturing CapEx, while gross debt climbed to $49.50 billion. When a company must spend that heavily just to defend supply and replace future patent cliffs, headline non-GAAP earnings overstate true owner cash flow.

That is why our valuation framework anchors on 48.0 times normalized 2027 free cash flow rather than today's 65.5 times trailing multiple. Using 48.0x FCF gives us a $1,450.00 Base Fair Value, compared with a $1,050.00 Bear Case if GLP-1 prices fall 20 percent and recurring IPR&D persists. Weighting 25 percent Bull ($1,720.00), 50 percent Base ($1,450.00), and 25 percent Bear ($1,050.00) yields an Expected Value of $1,417.50—hardly enough to justify paying $1,347.11 with tirzepatide at 65.9 percent of revenue and Trulicity and Verzenio entering 2028 IRA price-setting.

callouts.title: The Valuation Bottom Line
callouts.text: Great science does not override entry math. Paying 65.5x free cash flow for 65.9% single-molecule concentration and -15% realized price erosion leaves only +7.6% upside to our $1,450.00 base fair value.
